# 1 Clement Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 12 concludes the OT faith-gallery with Rahab, the only named woman in the positive examples. Her twofold virtue — faith *and* hospitality (*philoxenia*) — mirrors Abraham's (10:6) and Lot's (11:1). Clement presents Rahab as an outsider (a Canaanite prostitute) saved by her active welcome of God's agents, paralleling how the Ninevites (7:7) were outsiders saved by their response to God's word.

The typological interpretation of the scarlet cord (v.7) — as a sign of Christ's blood — is among the earliest examples of explicit christological typology applied to this text. Justin Martyr also makes this connection (Dialogue with Trypho 111). The cord becomes a proto-sacramental sign.

Note: "harlot/prostitute" (*pornē*) — all three agents agree this is the correct rendering; there is no warrant for softening it to "innkeeper" (as some ancient interpreters did).

---

## Chapter 12

**12:1** Because of her faith and hospitality Rahab the harlot was saved. [Josh 2; 6]

**12:2** For when the spies were sent to Jericho by Joshua the son of Nun, the king of the land learned that they had come to reconnoiter his country, and sent men to seize them in order to put them to death.

**12:3** But the hospitable Rahab took them in and hid them under the stalks of flax on the roof.

**12:4** And when the king's messengers came and said, "The spies who came to our land came in to you; bring them out, for so the king commands," she answered: "The two men whom you seek left me and went away" — and she directed them on a different road.

**12:5** And she said to the men: "I know full well that the LORD your God is delivering this city into your hands, for fear and dread of you has fallen upon all its inhabitants. When therefore you take it, keep me and my father's household safe."

**12:6** And they said to her: "It shall be exactly as you have spoken to us. When you perceive that we are coming, gather all your household under your roof, and they shall be saved; but whoever is found outside your house shall perish."

**12:7** And they gave her a sign: she was to hang a scarlet cord from her house — making manifest that through the blood of the Lord redemption would come to all who believe and hope in God.

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
